explanation: The second attack on Ugentana happened because the first one had not finished the job, and the article about the second says so in its own words. “Battle of Ugentana (1536)”, at revision 1373045056, § The Battle: “In 1535, the Portuguese captain of Malacca Dom Estevão da Gama attempted to defeat the Sultan of Johor by attacking his capital at Ugentana. Although he burned the city, the sultan avoided the total destruction of his forces by evacuating the city and retreating with his army into the jungle, while most of his fleet was out at sea at the time. Hence, he was able to rebuild his city and continue harassing the navigation of Malacca after the Portuguese had left, and for that reason Dom Estevão was compelled to try and attack Ugentana once more.” The same section carries the mechanism twice more, in the state the first attack left the ground in: the Portuguese found “a new stockade where a stone fort they destroyed the previous year had once stood”, and “the sultan’s forces were considerably weakened because the Portuguese had captured large amounts of artillery the previous year.” The second author is the record at the other end of this edge, “Battle of Ugentana” at revision 1373042668, which states the half the first article is reasoning from: “Unable to oppose the Portuguese, the sultan ordered the evacuation of the fort and also his capital under the cover of the night, and fled into the jungle”, and the city “was then burned”. `caused`, running forward from the incomplete victory to the campaign sent to complete it; `probable`, on the two articles alone, which rule 22 keeps below `consensus`.
